Hi Connor / Marissa —

Thanks for the quick responses in the call earlier. We're excited to get the hands-on session started. A few asks from our side so we can finalize logistics:

- Can we confirm a hybrid setup (2 onsite engineers + 3 remote) for Wed 2/16? Prefer morning (10:00 PT) so our EU folks can join late morning.
- We will need visitor badges for two Redwoods on site (names to follow) and the main meeting room reserved with projector + HDMI.
- Important: we want to run a short prompt dry-run (20 minutes) and then a load window (45 minutes). Our ops team will need to know the target throughput and whether you prefer a single steady stream or ramp tests.

I'll attach the prompt set we'll start with — see Prompt_set_v1.csv. Also adding Tom (IT Ops) for badge & network questions.

Best,
Elena

Elena — thanks for the clear list. Wed 2/16 10:00 PT should work from our side, but I wanted to check two things before I lock room and badges:

1) Would you prefer the session recorded for internal review? We typically ask customers to sign-off on recording — we can mark "no recording" if you'd rather keep it off.
2) For the load window: do you want us to aim for a steady 60 concurrent requests (low-latency focus) or a ramp from 10 to 200 qps to stress batch/throughput? Both are doable but they change GPU and queueing config.

Marissa — can you book the SF lab (Room B, 4th floor) with projector + HDMI and request 2 visitor badges for the morning of 2/16 (arrive 09:30, depart 14:30)? Also please schedule a short AV check with Ops on 2/15 at 16:00 PT.

Thanks,
Connor

Tom / Elena — quick note on the load profile so Ops can prep:

- For the workshop we recommend a two-step plan: 1) prompt dry-run (10–20 min) with 10–20 concurrent sessions using the attached Prompt_set_v1.csv to validate prompt/formatting, and 2) a throughput window (45 min) with a stepped ramp: 10 qps -> 60 qps steady -> 180 qps peak for 5 min, then back to steady.
- Target latency SLO: p95 < 300ms for the steady 60 qps configuration.
- We'll run the test from our dedicated lab GPU pool (A100-equivalent). If you prefer a tunnel into Fintegrate, that will require pre-approved firewall rules; otherwise guest VLAN with NAT is fine for synthetic load.

Please confirm preferred ramp profile and if Fintegrate wants to inject live customer-like prompts vs. synthetic.

Rishi
Rishi Malhotra
Sr. Performance Engineer, Redwood Inference
